newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIA LATE PALM OLEIN STABLE, TENDER CANCELLED.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIA LATE PALM OLEIN STABLE, TENDER CANCELLED.

text.p: Indonesian palm olein prices were stable in late trading on Friday on steady demand, while a crude palm oil tender was cancelled because the top bid was below the seller's expectations, trader said.

They said palm olein was traded at 1,470-75 rupiah/kg in Jakarta, unchanged from the opening. A 500-tonne crude palm oil tender in the North Sumatran city of Medan was cancelled for the second time. The top bid was 1,220 rupiah/kg but the seller was seeking 1,226 rupiah. It will be re-tendered next week.
"The cancellation of the tender goes to show that sellers are calling the shots," one trader said. "Supply is tight, and is expected to get even tighter next week."
Traders said the tight supply was due to soaring exports to Europe, where prices were at a premium to local values.
They said many players closed early on Friday in anticipation of further gains next week.
"Many players stopped selling because they expect prices to go up next week," one trader said. "Some players are also out of oil and are awaiting fresh shipments."

The traders said there was market talk of state logistics agency BULOG importing palm olein from Malaysia, but this could not be confirmed. BULOG intervenes in the market when prices exceed the 1,500-rupiah level.
Data from Belawan Port showed that MT Istana-I was scheduled to arrive at the north Sumatran port on Friday from Palembang with 1,503 tonnes of crude palm oil.
